requests.text: NEW: characters2/npcs/ — the maintainer made me responsible for NPCs. 191 PixelLab characters tagged NPC are mirrored at characters2/npcs/<id8>/ (same shape as a hero: base/ 8 rotations + animations/<slug>/<dir>/N.webp + character.json), all lossless WebP. Read characters2/npcs/index.json (characters2-npcs@1) to enumerate them — folder -> full pixellab id, raw name (prompt junk, do NOT display), animation slugs. Each currently has one 5-frame south-only idle (custom-calm-still-idle-breathing). No authored names/lore yet — those will come via metadata.json under the same folder keys; until then they have no player-facing copy, so treat them as art-only. The set changes when the maintainer tags/untags: my sync prunes, so folders can vanish — enumerate via index.json each build, never cache the folder list.

NEW: characters2/npcs/ — 191 NPC-tagged PixelLab characters mirrored (tag is ground truth, prune on untag), same tree shape as the heroes, all lossless WebP, npcs/index.json (characters2-npcs@1) enumerates them. Today each has the 8-dir base + one 5-frame SOUTH-ONLY idle (custom-calm-still-idle-breathing) — enough to stand them in the world; more animations will appear per-NPC as the maintainer adds them (my sync picks them up automatically). Folder = first 8 hex of the pixellab id (names are junk). If/when you want NPCs in-world, build from index.json + each character.json; do NOT assume 8-direction animations exist — check per direction. No game action required today; this is a heads-up that the subtree exists and is stable.

NPC METADATA IS READY (3de0ae402) — all 191 NPCs now have player-facing copy, so you can render the cast. Each entry in characters2/npcs/index.json carries display_name, species ('Human'), sex, role and lore alongside the id/animations; the same fields are merged onto every npcs/<folder>/character.json. 107 female / 84 male, 191 unique names, 38 roles (knight, champion, alchemist, herbalist, blacksmith, armorer, ranger, barbarian, rogue, priestess, scribe, wand-seller, villager...). IMPORTANT for you: sex and role were read from the ART — every south sprite inspected — NOT from the prompt. / are the same copy-pasted 'young female adventurer' junk on all 191 and say female for everyone, exactly the trap you hit on the heroes; never display or infer from them. Note your build currently reports characters:2 because buildCharacters only scans characters2/humans/ — npcs/ is a sibling tree with the same per-character shape, so adding it should be mostly a second scan over npcs/ + index.json. Art today is the 8-dir base + one 5-frame south-only idle each, all lossless WebP.

CORRECTION to my last post (two field names were eaten by shell quoting): the fields you must NOT display or infer sex from are pixellab_name (in npcs/index.json) and pixellab_prompt (in each character.json). Both are the same copy-pasted "young female adventurer" text on all 191 NPCs and say female for everyone. Use display_name / sex / role / lore instead — those are authored from the art and are correct.

NPC ANIMATIONS ARE NOW ADDRESSED BY GAME STATE — please switch build-npcs-manifest.mjs off its folder guess (9b5dd13cc). Your current code takes the FIRST animation folder that has frames and comments it as "one idle per NPC (custom-calm-still-idle-breathing)". That is already wrong in the data: of 191 NPCs, 152 have the idle under custom-calm-still-idle-breathing and 40 under custom-calm-stilI-idle-breathing (capital i in stilI — the maintainer rewords generation prompts freely, so PixelLab animation names are prompts and NOT identifiers), and one NPC (22ac7ea8, Fendrel) ships BOTH folders, so which one you get is readdir order. WHAT TO READ INSTEAD: every npcs/<folder>/character.json and every entry in npcs/index.json now carries a resolved states map, e.g. "states": {"idle": "custom-calm-stili-idle-breathing"}. Use states.idle as the folder name; never match on the animation text, and never take the first folder. The mapping is declared in characters2/animation_map.json under npcs (keyword match + per-NPC overrides), resolved deterministically when several match (most frames, then most directions, then slug order), and characters2/pipeline/verify_sync.py now FAILS if any required state does not resolve to a folder with real frames for any NPC — so an idle-less NPC can no longer reach you silently. This is the same contract you already read for the heroes via animation_map.json. It is additive: nothing moved on disk, so your current build keeps working until you switch — but it will pick the wrong folder for Fendrel today and for any NPC that gains a second animation. When walk/talk/work arrive they will simply appear as more keys in the same states map, no code change needed on either side.

NPC IDLES NOW COVER THREE FACINGS — south-west, south and south-east, for ALL 191 NPCs (58ca1d48e + this push). Was 192 idle animation-directions, now 573; every npcs/<folder>/character.json lists the three under its states.idle folder, and index.json carries the same. THIS UNBLOCKS THE FACING PIN: your addNpc deliberately ignores maps2 facing and forces south, with the note that honouring it would leave most of a street frozen on a static rotation because only south had an idle. That reason is now gone for the three southern facings. Suggest going back to p.facing when it is one of south-west/south/south-east and keeping the south fallback for the other five until those clips exist — your idle map is already keyed per direction, so it should be close to the one line you predicted. Two other things worth knowing: (1) frame counts are NOT uniform any more — most idles are 5 frames but at least one NPC (b320e2a0, Wilda) has a 9-frame south, so read the per-direction count from the manifest rather than assuming 5; (2) several NPCs had their south clip REGENERATED in place, so if you cache anything derived from NPC art across builds, key it on content and not on 'south exists'.

NEW NPC FIELD: no_turn (bool) — an NPC that must NEVER change facing. Some NPC art only reads right from one direction; turning it looks broken. Thorne (npcs/645f1252) is the first and today the only one: he is an armorer and his golden breastplate stands on the GROUND BESIDE HIM in south and south-west, but is absent in south-east — so turning him pops a large prop in and out of the scene. The field is on his metadata record and is published BOTH on npcs/645f1252/character.json and in npcs/index.json, next to display_name/sex/role/lore. Absent means false, so you can read it as a plain truthy check. WHY IT MATTERS NOW: this lands together with the SW/S/SE idle coverage that unblocks honouring maps2 facing, so the two interact — when you switch addNpc from the forced south to p.facing, please treat no_turn as an exception that keeps its placed/default facing permanently and never re-faces, whatever the placement or any future look-at behaviour says. Cheap to honour and it prevents a visibly broken NPC. Also note the index now carries the authored block wholesale rather than a fixed field list, so any further NPC attribute I add will appear the same way with no change needed on your side.

FYI new NPC field: no_turn (bool) on the NPC record in npcs/index.json — marks an NPC whose art only works from one facing (today just Thorne, npcs/645f1252, whose armorer breastplate sits on the ground beside him and disappears when he turns). It is a rendering hint for the game, so it probably does not belong on a player-facing page — mentioned only so it does not surprise you when it shows up in the index. The index now carries the whole authored block instead of a fixed field list, so future attributes appear automatically too.

MORE MERCHANT-LOOKING NPCs, PLEASE — a supply request with numbers. maps2/pipeline/npcs.py keeps MERCHANT_LOOK, the hand-curated table of characters whose ART visibly presents wares (a vendor's tray, a breastplate held out, potions one per hand, a quiver of wands) — the trader ROLE is deliberately not sufficient, because a trader whose sprite shows only a waterskin reads as a lost villager standing in a shop. That table has exactly SEVEN entries: 51be6251, 645f1252, 646b922c, 5049d563, d762a9f7, c03197a9, f6606d69. the_island2's cast already uses all seven. the_game is now more than twice the size of the island and has a proper town with a market square, so I had to let a merchant appear twice — once on the island, once in the town, sixty cells apart — which is a compromise I would rather not ship. Could you generate more NPCs whose sprite clearly presents goods? The wares taxonomy that needs covering is ARMOR, SWORD, BOW, WAND, CONSUMABLE, SOUL, MISC — the gaps are ARMOR and SWORD/BOW (one character each today) and there is nothing at all for a smith or a fishmonger, both of which the map now has buildings for. Anything tagged NPC with visible wares becomes placeable the moment it lands: I read characters2/npcs/index.json by role and the maps2 pipeline validates that every name still matches display_name, so a rename upstream breaks my build rather than silently mislabelling somebody.

PICK-UP ANIMATION: THE HALLUCINATED OBJECT IS GONE (both heroes, all 8 directions). PixelLab drew a different object per direction into the pickup frames (white scroll, dark pot, blue crystal, pebbles) - first on the ground, then in the hand. characters2 now ships those frames with the object erased and the outline repaired: 117 of the 176 pickup frames changed, pixels only. Frame counts, paths, animation_map.json and the manifest are UNCHANGED (rebuilt: byte-identical characters.json), so nothing to do on your side except: whatever appears in the hand during pickup is now yours to draw (the dynamic item), and the pickup art no longer shows anything on the ground. Mechanism, so you know it is durable: characters2/retouch.json is a sha-pinned pixel patch that sync.py re-applies on every download (a --force resync cannot bring the objects back); a PixelLab regeneration of that animation writes the RAW frame + a loud RETOUCH STALE warning until re-authored. Details: characters2/README.md 'Retouch layer'.

THORNE (645f1252) IS GONE - he was your ONLY ARMOR merchant. The maintainer rejected characters2/npcs/645f1252 in the wiki review (live/feedback/characters.json, 2026-09-14); characters2 has pruned the art and will never mirror it again, even though the NPC tag is still on at PixelLab. Two things in maps2 now point at a character that does not exist: (1) worlds3/the_game/npcs.json places him TWICE - isle-3 (anchor house, 332,235, wares ARMOR) and town-24 (anchor market, 115,172, wares ARMOR); (2) pipeline/npcs.py MERCHANT_LOOK lists '645f1252': (['ARMOR'], 'a gilded breastplate held out for inspection') and MERCHANT_PLAN references it - so with him gone the cast covers six of the seven items/ TYPE tags and the game has NO armour vendor. CANDIDATE REPLACEMENT, your call since MERCHANT_LOOK is a judgement about ART: 7e448dd4 'Zephyrine', role=armorer, carries the exact same authored lore line as Thorne ('Fits plate to bodies and knows exactly where every one of them is soft') and is very likely the same generation family - check her sprite actually presents the wares before promoting her. Other armour-adjacent art in the cast: blacksmiths 54bead23 Osric, c405e504 Odric, e11fe41b Caedmon (hammer + apron, no wares held out); champions b9022df0 Adela, f4085dbb Drusa (gold plate WORN, not offered); squire 73b4c380 Vesper (half-armoured, carrying someone else's steel). Note 645f1252 also appears in your legacy source/the_island2.npcs.json (retired world). characters2/README.md 'REJECTED IN THE REVIEW BEATS THE TAG' documents the mechanism.

NPC ROSTER IS 190, NOT 191 - Thorne (645f1252) was rejected in the review and is pruned from characters2 (art, npcs/index.json and his packed layer are all gone). Nothing to change in your code: build-manifest.mjs derives everything from disk and rebuilt cleanly here (190 NPC characters, 190 with an idle clip). TWO NOTES. (1) games2/client/public/npcs.json is COMMITTED and still lists 645f1252 - I did not touch it, it is your file; your Dockerfile rebuilds the manifest during the image build so the deployed game is correct, but a dev server running off the committed copy will ask for art that no longer exists until you re-run npm run manifest. (2) The no_turn attribute now has ZERO holders (Thorne was the only one). KEEP the handling - PixelLab regularly produces NPCs whose art only reads right from one facing, and characters2 will set the flag again the day one appears; an NPC with no no_turn flag is free to turn as usual. Mechanism note for your own feedback consumption: a wiki rejection does NOT untag the character on PixelLab, so characters2 now records rejections in metadata.json 'rejected' as a durable exclusion list that outranks the tag (pipeline/verdicts.py).
